reviewed.references: m1n1 pmgr.c and pcie.c at the pinned 121fcbf3, dart.c/dart8020.py, the XNU IOService.cpp and config/*.exports in sources/puredarwin-m1-desktop, and the saved-ADT result in source-validation.json.

verdict: APPROVE revision 002 for root's later packet work, with no hardware implied. The read path is an exact allowlist behind a full power/clock guard before every DART read. Maps are lazy, read-only, inhibit-cache and released before publication. The 764-byte V1 diagnostic is copied once and set on the persistent IOResources provider with plain setProperty on every completed refusal or success path. The one-shot claim prevents rematch repeats. The built bundle's every import except the baseline dyld_stub_binder is covered by a declared KPI. No defects; notes S1-S6.
board_guard: Exact identity: root target-type 'J293', compatible 'J293AP\0MacBookPro17,1\0AppleARM', arm-io 'arm-io,t8103', apcie 'apcie,t8103', dart-apcie0 'dart,t8020', pmgr 'pmgr1,t8103', aic 'aic,1'. All are exact byte compares including NUL; properties must be non-null and at most 32 KiB.

Registers: apcie reg must be exactly 21 tuples, with idx1 RC 0x680000000/0x4000, idx2 PHY 0x680080000/0x90000 and idx6 port0 0x681000000/0x8000. dart-apcie0 reg is 1 tuple 0x681008000/0x4000; pmgr reg is 54 tuples with idx0 0x23b700000/0x8c000. Addresses resolve through /arm-io ranges (24-byte tuples, at most 32). Every covering tuple must give the same physical answer, all sums are overflow-checked, and the arm-io base is never re-added to already-physical APCIE entries.

PMGR: devices are 48-byte entries matching m1n1 struct pmgr_device (flags@0, parent[2]@4, addr_offset@10, psreg_idx@11, id@26, name@32). ps-regs are 12-byte entries. For IMX 32, APCIE 77 (parent 32), APCIE_GP 97 (parent 77) and PCIE_REF 29 the guard requires a unique id, the non-virtual flag (0x10 clear), the exact parent with parent[1] = 0 and the exact name. Each address = reg[psreg.reg] + psreg.offset + addr_offset*8, the same formula as m1n1 pmgr_device_get_addr (:139-156), resolving to 0x23b7001b8, 0x348, 0x3e8 and 0x1a0, inside the 0x4000 map prefix.

Device facts: apcie clock-gates and power-gates [77,97,29], bus-range [0,8], #ports 3. dart-apcie0 page-size 0x4000, vm-base 0x100000, vm-size 0xbfe00000, dart-options 0x17, manual-availability 1, interrupts 696, interrupt-parent equal to the AIC's nonzero AAPL,phandle.

The adapter's property callback copies each ADT OSData into a per-start OSArray (cap 128; this validator makes about 37 lookups), so borrowed pointers stay valid. The array is released before any MMIO. IORegistryEntry::fromPath(path, gIODTPlane) resolves '/' to the device-tree root and then child names, per XNU fromPath.
read_allowlist_and_guard: dls_read_allowed is exact. PMGR: only 0x1b8, 0x348, 0x3e8, 0x1a0. PHY: only 0x0. RC: only 0x24. Port: only 0x800, 0x804, 0x814. DART: 0x00, 0x04, 0x60, 0xfc, 0x80-0x8c, 0x100-0x13c and 0x200-0x2fc, all 4-byte aligned. Nothing else, so no command, selector, error/ack or DAPF register can be read. read32 rechecks the allowlist and region bounds before mapping, and the r >= DLS_REGIONS case short-circuits before the board.size index.

The PMGR guard matches pinned m1n1 pmgr.c:9-17. It refuses RESET bit31, AUTO_ENABLE bit28, PARENT_OFF bit11, DEV_DISABLE bit10 and also bit12 (see S6), and requires TARGET[3:0] = ACTUAL[7:4] = 0xf. WAS_CLKGATED/WAS_PWRGATED (bits 9/8) are history and allowed.

PHY/RC/port checks match pinned m1n1 pcie.c:38-69. APCIE_PHY_CTRL CLK0REQ/CLK1REQ/CLK0ACK/CLK1ACK (bits 0-3) must all be set and RESET_T8103 bit7 clear. PHYIF_CTRL 0x24 RUN, PORT_APPCLK 0x800 EN, PORT_STATUS 0x804 RUN and PORT_RESET 0x814 DIS each require bit0.

Sequence: every DART read is preceded by a fresh 9-read guard. A final guard is required for DLS_SAMPLED, giving 88 samples x 10 + 9 = 889 reads, capped at 1024. Page shift other than 14 (PARAMS1 bits 27:24), CONFIG LOCK bit15 or enabled-stream bits above 15 stop as UNSUPPORTED. Any I/O error or unmet prerequisite stops immediately: no retry, no write path (the dls_io interface has only read32), and no pointer formed from a sampled value. Offsets match m1n1 (CONFIG 0x60 lock 15, ENABLED_STREAMS 0xfc, REMAP irange(0x80,4,4), TCR irange(0x100,16,4), TTBR 16x4 at 0x200 stride 16) and Linux PARAMS1.
maps: mapRegion is reached only from read32 after allowlist and bounds checks, so the DART region is first mapped after a full successful guard. Mapping uses IOMemoryDescriptor::withPhysicalAddress(base, 0x4000, kIODirectionIn) and map(kIOMapAnywhere | kIOMapInhibitCache | kIOMapReadOnly), requiring a nonzero VA and size >= 0x4000. The load is a single volatile const uint32_t between 'dmb osh' barriers. releaseMaps runs in synchronous start before the diagnostic copy and in free(), map then descriptor, in reverse region order, idempotently. No mapping outlives start.
diagnostic_ownership: One OSData::withBytes(&snapshot, 764) copy is made after releaseMaps. provider->setProperty('PDDARTSurveyDiagnosticV1', data) and setProperty('PDDARTSurveyObservationV1', data) are separately tracked. IOLog reports diagnostic_copy, provider_preserved and instance_recorded without changing snapshot.result. start returns false on refusal, missing copy or failed recording, after super::stop. IOKit then detaches and frees the instance, while IOResources keeps its own retained reference in its property table.

IOResources overrides only setProperties (the user-client path, IOService.cpp:7619), not IORegistryEntry::setProperty. The kernel-side setProperty therefore neither publishes a resource nor calls registerService. Paths that return before the board validator (boot argument, attempted, super::start failure) record nothing; this is documented.
Every path reaches the copy: board refusal (snapshot version 1, result, failure_region = 5), sampling refusal or error, and success. stop and free never remove the provider property.
abi_764: observation_layout.h asserts sizeof(dls_sample) = 8, sizeof(dls_snapshot) = 764, align 4, and the offsets version 0 / sample_count 4 / reads 8 / region 12 / offset 16 / result 20 / power 24 / clocks 40 / samples 60. These are static_assert in the C++ adapter and _Static_assert in C. The SDK build succeeding means they held for the ARM64 target. The bundle's start passes 0x2fc (764) to OSData::withBytes.
rematch_and_notifiers: The personality matches IOResources with IOResourceMatch IOKit and a unique IOMatchCategory. probe requires pddartsurvey=1 and wins OSCompareAndSwap(0,1) on a never-cleared global (__bss gSurveyClaimed). Later IOResources re-registrations may instantiate the class again, but probe returns nullptr with no MMIO. On success registerService publishes only this diagnostic service; nothing matches PDDARTSurvey as provider. No notifier, timer, interrupt or workloop is installed. The antimain pd_dart_survey_stop returns KERN_FAILURE.

sdk_bundle.kpi_coverage: All 309 undefined symbols except dyld_stub_binder are exported by the declared bundles: 239 from kpi.iokit (IOKit.exports, including PE_parse_boot_argn, gIODTPlane, IOLog, IOMemoryDescriptor::withPhysicalAddress, the IORegistryEntry/IOService vtable entries) and 69 from kpi.libkern (OSCompareAndSwap, OSData/OSArray, bzero, memcmp, memcpy, memset, strlen, ___cxa_atexit, OSObject typed new/delete). kpi.mach and kpi.unsupported are declared but not needed by any import, which is harmless.
sdk_bundle.baseline: dyld_stub_binder, ___cxa_atexit, _memcpy and a __mod_init_func section appear identically in the hardware-qualified PDM1SPIHID SDK005 (4d7aa91f), so they are SDK toolchain baseline, not new to this kext.
sdk_bundle.start_path: Strings carry the exact property names, boot argument, IOLog format and ADT paths. Disassembly of PDDARTSurvey::start shows dls_validate_board -> dls_sample -> releaseMaps -> OSData::withBytes(..., 764) -> two virtual setProperty calls -> IOLog, in source order. gSurveyClaimed is a __bss global; kmod_info and the antimain are present.

tests: Not rerun here. Root's receipt: 6 groups, 889 read-fault positions, 88 power-loss boundaries, 8 compiled mutants rejected, NDEBUG refused, saved-ADT board guard PASS, 40 publication combinations. The rev002 diff touches no sampler, guard or allowlist code (board.c, survey.c and survey.h are unchanged from revision 001).

notes.text: PDDARTSurveyDiagnosticV1 sits on IOResources, which any IORegistry reader can see. It includes raw TTBR words (physical addresses of firmware tables) and TCR/remap values. That is acceptable for this single-user diagnostic boot as private evidence, but it must never ship in a general build. The key also becomes a matchable IOResourceMatch name at the next IOResources re-registration; no personality uses it.

mapRegion leaves partial state on failure. If map() fails, descriptors[r] stays set (a second call would overwrite and leak it). If the map is undersized or has VA 0, maps[r] stays set and a second call would return true. This is unreachable today because the sampler never retries after DLS_IO and releaseMaps frees both. Clear both on failure if a retry is ever added.

Matching on IOResources/IOKit runs early in boot. If m1n1/HV has not left APCIE domains, PHY clocks and port0 running, the guard records NOT_READY (fail-closed, with diagnostic). If firmware sets AUTO_ENABLE on these domains, the survey refuses by design.
There is no protection against a synchronous MMIO abort or hang (documented): a callback bound cannot interrupt a load. Root's bounded runtime plan and recovery must cover this.
registerService on success publishes a generic IOService. Nothing matches it today. Keep it unmatched (no personality may use PDDARTSurvey as provider) so that success never triggers driver loading.

The PMGR refusal mask includes bit12, called 'PS_RESET' in the README. Pinned m1n1 pmgr.c defines only bits 31, 28, 27:24, 11, 10, 9, 8 and the state fields, and no pinned reference names bit12. Refusing it is fail-closed: at worst it yields a spurious NOT_READY. Record it as an unattributed conservative refusal, or cite a pinned source.
